name: Parallax Hearth
description: Parallax Hearth is a gentle world of chalk hills and wide, slow rivers that meander through valleys blanketed in amber grass. Underground cavern systems honeycomb the planet's upper crust, carved by subterranean rivers over billions of years. Petrified forests crown the higher plateaus, their stone trunks preserving the memory of an ancient arboreal epoch that ended long before any survey ship arrived.

The lower gravity lends a languid quality to movement on Parallax Hearth, where dust motes hang in the air and waterfalls seem to fall in slow motion. The atmosphere is clean and carries the mineral tang of chalk dust, particularly during the dry months when the hills shed their surface layers in gentle erosion. Sunsets last for hours, painting the sky in bands of peach and violet.

A colonial settlement was established here two centuries ago but was abandoned within a generation under mysterious circumstances. The buildings remain standing, eerily preserved by the dry climate, with personal effects still arranged as though their owners simply walked away. The native fauna, small mammalian herbivores with six limbs, have since moved into the abandoned structures, nesting in the ruins of human ambition.

The fauna of Parallax Hearth face extinction pressure from an introduced pathogen believed to have arrived with the original colonists. Conservation teams are working to develop treatments, but funding remains scarce for a world with limited strategic value. The mystery of the colony's abandonment continues to draw investigators, some of whom suspect the pathogen's origin may hold the key to understanding what drove the settlers away.
